q: Who wrote the tragedy Romeo and Juliet?
x: The play was probably written in the mid-1590s and is based on an earlier Italian tale. It is set in Verona.

q: Who wrote the novel Pride and Prejudice?
x: Published in 1813, it was first issued anonymously, credited only to 'the Author of Sense and Sensibility'.

q: Which author created the detective Sherlock Holmes?
x: Doyle was a physician. He based Holmes partly on Joseph Bell, a doctor known for his sharp powers of deduction.

q: Who is the author of the Harry Potter series?
x: Rowling reportedly conceived the idea for Harry while on a delayed train from Manchester to London in 1990.

q: Who wrote The Hobbit?
x: Published in 1937, it began as a story Tolkien told his children. He reportedly scribbled its first line on an exam paper.

q: In Moby-Dick, what is the name of the captain obsessed with the white whale?
x: Captain Ahab commands the whaling ship Pequod. He lost a leg to the whale on an earlier voyage.

q: Who wrote A Christmas Carol?
x: Dickens wrote this ghost story in just a few weeks in 1843, and it was published that December.

q: In Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, what does Alice follow down the hole?
x: The rabbit pulls a pocket watch from his waistcoat and says he is late. Alice follows out of curiosity.

q: Who wrote The Great Gatsby?
x: The novel was published in 1925. It is set on Long Island during the Jazz Age.

q: Who wrote To Kill a Mockingbird?
x: It appeared in 1960 and won the 1961 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. Lee drew on her childhood in Alabama.

q: Who wrote the dystopian novel 1984?
x: Published in 1949, it introduced phrases like Big Brother and Newspeak into everyday language.

q: In Animal Farm, what kind of animal is the leader Napoleon?
x: Orwell's 1945 fable satirizes the Russian Revolution. Napoleon is a boar who seizes control of the farm.

q: Who wrote The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe?
x: Lewis and Tolkien were friends and belonged to the same Oxford writing group, the Inklings.

q: Which Spanish author wrote Don Quixote?
x: Part one appeared in 1605 and part two in 1615. It is often called the first modern novel.

q: Which Italian poet wrote The Divine Comedy?
x: Dante completed it around 1320, and its three parts are Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso.

q: Which ancient Greek poet is traditionally credited with composing the Odyssey?
x: Tradition says Homer was blind, but little is known about him. Scholars still debate whether one poet composed both the Iliad and the Odyssey.

q: In Shakespeare's Hamlet, Hamlet is the prince of which country?
x: The play is set at Elsinore castle. Shakespeare based the story on an old Danish legend about Amleth.

q: Which Shakespeare play features the moneylender Shylock?
x: Shylock demands a pound of flesh as payment for an unpaid loan. The famous courtroom scene follows.

q: Who wrote Frankenstein?
x: Shelley began the story at age 18 during a rainy summer holiday in Switzerland, after a ghost-story challenge among friends.

q: Which author wrote the vampire novel Dracula?
x: Stoker's novel was published in 1897. Its Transylvanian count helped shape nearly every vampire story since.

q: Who wrote Little Women?
x: Alcott based the four March sisters on herself and her own sisters. The book came out in 1868.

q: Which author wrote The Adventures of Tom Sawyer?
x: Published in 1876, it draws on Twain's boyhood in Hannibal, Missouri, on the Mississippi River.

q: In Oliver Twist, what does Oliver famously ask for more of?
x: His request, 'Please, sir, I want some more,' shocks the workhouse master. It is one of the best-known scenes in Dickens.

q: Who wrote The Wonderful Wizard of Oz?
x: The book was published in 1900. Baum went on to write thirteen more Oz books.

q: Who wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory?
x: Dahl was a former fighter pilot. The book was published in 1964 and has been filmed twice.

q: Which children's author wrote The Cat in the Hat?
x: Seuss wrote it in 1957 using only a limited list of simple words, as a livelier alternative to dull school readers.

q: Who wrote Winnie-the-Pooh?
x: Milne named the bear after his son's teddy, and a real Canadian bear named Winnipeg also inspired the name.

q: Which Scottish author created Peter Pan?
x: Peter Pan first appeared in a 1904 play. Barrie left the rights to Great Ormond Street Hospital in London.

q: How many dwarfs live with Snow White in the classic fairy tale?
x: The Brothers Grimm gave the dwarfs no names. Names such as Doc and Grumpy came from the 1937 Disney film.

q: What does Cinderella lose as she flees the ball in the classic tale?
x: The glass slipper comes from Charles Perrault's 1697 version. In the Grimm version, the slipper is gold.

q: Which Danish author wrote The Ugly Duckling and The Emperor's New Clothes?
x: Andersen published his first fairy tales in 1835. Many of his stories, including The Little Mermaid, were original creations.

q: Which Greek hero spends ten years trying to get home after the Trojan War?
x: His long voyage is the subject of Homer's Odyssey. He is also known by his Roman name, Ulysses.

q: In Greek mythology, who is the king of the gods?
x: Zeus rules from Mount Olympus and wields the thunderbolt. His Roman counterpart is Jupiter.

q: Which legendary British king ruled from Camelot with his Knights of the Round Table?
x: The round table was said to remove any rank among the knights. Arthur's sword Excalibur is also part of the legend.

q: Who wrote The Catcher in the Rye?
x: Published in 1951, it is narrated by the restless teenager Holden Caulfield. Salinger later withdrew from public life.

q: Who wrote the novella Of Mice and Men?
x: Steinbeck took the title from a poem by Robert Burns. The story follows two migrant workers in California.

q: Which French author wrote Les Miserables?
x: Hugo finished the huge novel in exile in 1862. It follows the ex-convict Jean Valjean.

q: Who wrote The Three Musketeers?
x: Dumas serialized it in 1844. Fittingly, the hero d'Artagnan is not one of the three musketeers at first.

q: Which Russian author wrote War and Peace?
x: The novel is set during Napoleon's invasion of Russia. First published in installments in the 1860s, it runs well over a thousand pages.

q: Who wrote Crime and Punishment?
x: Published in 1866, it follows a poor student in St. Petersburg who commits a murder and wrestles with his guilt.

q: Which French author wrote Around the World in Eighty Days?
x: Verne's 1872 adventure follows Phileas Fogg on a wager. Verne is often called a father of science fiction.

q: Who wrote the pirate adventure Treasure Island?
x: Stevenson began the story by drawing a map of an island for his stepson. It introduced the one-legged pirate Long John Silver.

q: Who wrote the novel Jane Eyre?
x: It was published in 1847 under the pen name Currer Bell. The tale was an immediate success.

q: Who wrote Wuthering Heights?
x: Her only novel appeared in 1847 under the pen name Ellis Bell. Emily died the following year.

q: In The Lord of the Rings, which hobbit carries the One Ring to Mount Doom?
x: Frodo is Bilbo's nephew and heir. His loyal friend Sam accompanies him on the final stretch.

q: In Harry Potter, what is the name of the school of witchcraft and wizardry Harry attends?
x: Hogwarts is divided into four houses: Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw and Slytherin.

q: Which Irish-born author wrote Gulliver's Travels?
x: Published in 1726, this satire was a sharp attack on the politics and society of Swift's day, not simply a children's book.

q: Which English author wrote Robinson Crusoe?
x: Published in 1719, it is often considered one of the first English novels. It was inspired partly by a real castaway, Alexander Selkirk.

q: Which British author wrote The Jungle Book?
x: Kipling was born in India. The 1894 stories follow Mowgli, a boy raised by wolves, alongside Baloo and Bagheera.

q: Who wrote The Little Prince?
x: The author was also an aviator. His 1943 story, often translated into hundreds of languages, begins with a pilot stranded in the desert.

q: Who wrote The Hunger Games?
x: Published in 2008, the book is set in Panem. Collins said she was inspired in part by the Greek myth of Theseus and the Minotaur.

q: In Macbeth, what supernatural trio prophesies that Macbeth will be king?
x: The witches meet Macbeth and Banquo on a heath. Their predictions set the tragedy in motion.

q: Which American writer penned the poem The Raven?
x: Poe published it in 1845. Its refrain, 'Nevermore,' is spoken by the bird.

q: Which English poet wrote 'I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud'?
x: The poem, often called 'Daffodils', was inspired by a walk Wordsworth took with his sister Dorothy in the Lake District.

q: What syllable pattern does a traditional haiku follow?
x: The haiku is a Japanese form. English haiku often keep the 5-7-5 pattern, though in Japanese it counts sounds rather than syllables.

q: How many lines does a sonnet traditionally have?
x: Shakespeare wrote 154 sonnets. The Italian and English forms arrange the 14 lines differently.

q: Which ancient Greek epic poem tells of the wrath of Achilles during the Trojan War?
x: The poem opens with the word 'wrath.' It covers only a few weeks near the end of the ten-year war.

q: Who wrote The Diary of a Young Girl, a famous account of hiding during World War II?
x: Anne wrote the diary in hiding in Amsterdam. Her father Otto, the only survivor of the family, had it published in 1947.

q: Which Brazilian author wrote The Alchemist?
x: Published in 1988, the story of the shepherd Santiago became one of the most translated books by a living author.

q: Which Dr. Seuss character tries to steal Christmas from the Whos of Whoville?
x: How the Grinch Stole Christmas! appeared in 1957. The Grinch's heart is said to be two sizes too small.

q: What is the name of the great lion who rules Narnia?
x: Aslan is the Narnian creator and king. His name is the Turkish word for lion.

q: In which Jane Austen novel do Elinor and Marianne Dashwood appear?
x: Austen's first published novel appeared in 1811. Elinor represents sense and Marianne sensibility.

q: What is the name of the sport Harry Potter plays on a broomstick?
x: A Quidditch team has seven players, and catching the Golden Snitch ends the match and earns 150 points.

q: In the fairy tale Rapunzel, what does she let down from her tower?
x: The Brothers Grimm included the tale in their 1812 collection. The name Rapunzel refers to a leafy plant, rampion.

q: In which Shakespeare play does the line 'To be, or not to be' appear?
x: It begins Hamlet's famous soliloquy in Act 3. It is perhaps the most quoted line in English drama.

q: Who wrote The Old Man and the Sea?
x: The novella won the 1953 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction. Hemingway received the Nobel Prize the following year.

q: Who wrote Fahrenheit 451, a novel about a future where books are burned?
x: The title refers to the temperature at which book paper is said to catch fire. Bradbury wrote it in the basement of a library.

q: Which Canadian author wrote The Handmaid's Tale?
x: The dystopian novel appeared in 1985 and is set in the Republic of Gilead. Atwood wrote much of it in West Berlin.

q: Who wrote the 1932 dystopian novel Brave New World?
x: The title comes from a line in Shakespeare's The Tempest. Huxley's novel imagines a society controlled by pleasure and conditioning.

q: Who wrote the science fiction novel The War of the Worlds?
x: Published in 1898, it describes a Martian invasion of England. A 1938 radio dramatization famously alarmed some listeners.

q: What is the name of Captain Nemo's submarine in Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea?
x: Verne's 1870 novel imagined an electric-powered submarine. A league is a distance unit, so the title is a distance traveled, not a depth.

q: Who wrote The Call of the Wild, a novel about a sled dog named Buck?
x: Set during the Klondike Gold Rush, the 1903 novel drew on London's own time in Canada's Yukon.

q: Which Mark Twain character travels down the Mississippi on a raft with the runaway Jim?
x: Huckleberry Finn was published in 1884 and is told in Huck's own dialect, a bold choice for its time.

q: Who is Sherlock Holmes's loyal friend and chronicler?
x: Watson narrates most of the Holmes stories. He is an army doctor wounded in Afghanistan.

q: Who is the villainous pirate captain in Peter Pan?
x: Hook lost his hand to Peter, who fed it to a crocodile. The croc enjoyed the taste and now follows Hook everywhere.

q: Which Canadian author wrote Anne of Green Gables?
x: Published in 1908, it is set on Prince Edward Island. Anne is an orphan mistakenly sent to an older brother and sister.

q: Who wrote the horse story Black Beauty?
x: Sewell wrote it in 1877 from her sickbed, as a plea for kinder treatment of horses. She died a few months after it was published.

q: Who wrote The Secret Garden?
x: Published in 1911, it follows Mary Lennox, a lonely orphan who finds a hidden walled garden in Yorkshire.

q: Which author and illustrator created Where the Wild Things Are?
x: The 1963 picture book follows a boy named Max. It won the Caldecott Medal in 1964.

q: Who wrote The Very Hungry Caterpillar?
x: The 1969 book has holes punched through its pages to show where the caterpillar has eaten.

q: In Roald Dahl's story, what does BFG stand for?
x: Dahl published The BFG in 1982. The giant blows dreams into children's bedrooms through a trumpet.

q: Who wrote the picture book The Giving Tree?
x: Published in 1964, it tells of a tree that gives everything it has to a boy. Silverstein also wrote Where the Sidewalk Ends.

q: Which English poet wrote the epic Paradise Lost?
x: Milton was blind when he dictated the poem, which was first published in 1667. It retells the story of Adam and Eve.

q: Which medieval English author wrote The Canterbury Tales?
x: Chaucer wrote it in the late 1300s in Middle English. It has pilgrims telling stories on the road to Canterbury.

q: In the Old English epic Beowulf, which monster does the hero fight first?
x: Grendel attacks the hall of King Hrothgar. Beowulf later fights Grendel's mother and a dragon.

q: Who wrote The Picture of Dorian Gray?
x: Published in 1890, it was Wilde's only novel. Its title character stays young while his portrait ages.

q: Which crime writer wrote Murder on the Orient Express?
x: Christie published it in 1934, and its detective is Hercule Poirot. She is among the best-selling novelists in history.

q: Who wrote the thriller The Da Vinci Code?
x: Brown's 2003 novel opens with a murder in the Louvre. It sparked a boom of conspiracy-themed thrillers.

q: Who wrote the Civil War novel Gone with the Wind?
x: Published in 1936, it won the Pulitzer Prize the next year. It was Mitchell's only novel published in her lifetime.

q: Who wrote Lord of the Flies?
x: Published in 1954, it follows a group of schoolboys stranded on an island. Golding received the Nobel Prize in 1983.

q: Who wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?
x: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of the Oxford mathematician Charles Dodgson. He first told the story on a boat trip in 1862.

q: Who wrote and illustrated The Tale of Peter Rabbit?
x: Potter first told the story in a letter to a sick child in 1893. She self-published it in 1901 before a publisher took it on.

q: In Charlotte's Web, what kind of animal is Charlotte?
x: Charlotte saves the pig Wilbur by weaving words into her web. E. B. White published the book in 1952.

q: Who wrote the novel The Kite Runner?
x: Published in 2003, it was Hosseini's debut. The story is set in Afghanistan and later in California.

q: Who wrote the adventure novel Life of Pi?
x: The 2001 novel won the Booker Prize in 2002. It tells of a boy stranded in a lifeboat with a Bengal tiger.

q: In Franz Kafka's The Metamorphosis, what does Gregor Samsa turn into?
x: Kafka's 1915 novella opens with Gregor waking to find the change. Kafka insisted the insect never be drawn on the cover.

q: In which Shakespeare play does the mischievous sprite Puck appear?
x: Puck, also called Robin Goodfellow, serves the fairy king Oberon. His mistake with a love potion drives the plot.

q: Which storyteller in One Thousand and One Nights tells tales to delay her execution?
x: She keeps the king curious by stopping each night on a cliffhanger. After 1,001 nights he spares her.

q: Which dragon guards the treasure of the Lonely Mountain in The Hobbit?
x: Smaug is killed by Bard the Bowman, who spots a bare patch in the dragon's armor. The Lonely Mountain is also called Erebor.

q: Which Wonderland character famously shouts 'Off with her head!'?
x: The Queen of Hearts is rarely actually seen carrying out her executions. The Red Queen is a different character from the sequel.
